post.description:
Calculates sales tax for one cart of up to 250 line items with the Ziptax rate engine. Nothing is stored: the returned cartId correlates the response with the request only.

**Sourcing.** The destination is resolved first and its sourcing rule decides where the cart is quoted: at the destination, or at the origin when the destination's rule is origin-based and the origin resolves into the same state. Origin sourcing never crosses a state line. A product line's own rate rules can override the cart's sourcing: the most granular state, statewide, county or conditional rule that sets isDestinationTaxType quotes the line at the destination (true) or the origin (false), still never across a state line.

**Lines.** General goods (no taxabilityCode, or 0) are quoted at the SALES_TAX total of the address the cart is quoted at. Shipping (10001) and handling (11000) follow that address's shipping taxability: Y taxes both, N neither, L handling only. Any other code is a product code and needs the product_rates entitlement. It is quoted with its product rate rules: the most granular rule that carries a value applies to the whole rate, and a place or tax-code rule applies once to the summed rate of the components it covers; a rule exempts the line when price x quantity, rounded to cents, is strictly above exemptOver or strictly below exemptUnder, and otherwise taxes the amount above taxablePortionOver, times percentTaxable, at effectiveTaxRate or the rate it applies to. Prepared food (41000, 41041) is quoted from its meal tax when meal tax applies, which takes precedence over the rate rules: a STATE_SPECIAL_TOTAL component replaces all sales tax, ADD_ON components are added on top, and an OCCUPATION_TAX component is added and the sales tax is charged on it too. tax.rate is the total rate the line collects.

**transactionDate.** Optional RFC 3339 date-time, defaulting to now. A date in a past month is quoted from that month's historical rates, with rate rules and meal tax dated on the exact day in the date's own offset. The current month or a later one is quoted from current rates. A past month whose tax_table rates the running service has not loaded uses the current tax_table rates, while SST states and other dated sources keep the month, and rate rules and meal tax stay dated on its own day. A date before the historical rates start, or one that is not RFC 3339, is rejected with 400 before any address is resolved. The response echoes it.

**Failures.** A destination that cannot be resolved fails the cart with 422 and is never quoted at the origin, which can be in another state. An origin that cannot be resolved falls back to the destination. A rate response without a SALES_TAX total fails with 500 rather than quoting 0%. A failed rate lookup names the line item it failed on.

**Billing.** Each distinct address the cart resolved is one geo request, however many taxability codes it is resolved with, and an address that resolved is billed even when a later line fails. The origin is resolved only when the cart or a line is sourced there, or for a prepared-food line, whose seller-located meal tax comes from it, unless the destination's meal tax already reports RULES_NOT_LOADED, LOCATION_NOT_RESOLVED or STATE_NOT_COVERED and the line is not due at the origin. The addresses are free-form strings, so the origin's state is known only once it resolves: an origin-sourced cart whose origin is in another state never resolves it again for a line, while on a destination-sourced cart such a line resolves, and bills, the origin to learn its state, even when it turns out to be in another state.

400.description: The request failed validation: a body that does not bind (error `Invalid request`, with details), more or fewer than one cart, no line items or more than 250, or a transactionDate that is not RFC 3339 or is older than the historical rates (error `Invalid request`, with details). Also a rate lookup the engine rejected as a malformed query or historical period (v60 105, 111), with details and itemId.

401.description: No X-API-KEY header (`Missing X-API-KEY header`), an invalid or inactive key (`Invalid or inactive API key`, with status), or a key the rate engine rejected (v60 101, `Invalid API key`, with details and itemId).

403.description: The key's plan does not include something the cart needs: address lookups (v60 107), international rates (112), or product rate rules for a line's taxabilityCode (113). With details and itemId.

422.description: The destination address could not be resolved (v60 102, 103, 104, 109, 110, or a result with no state): `destination address could not be resolved and a cart cannot be quoted without it`, with details and itemId. The cart is never quoted at its origin instead.

429.description: More than 100 requests a minute to the endpoint, across all callers, on one server instance (`Rate limit exceeded`, with message), or the account's usage quota is used up (v60 108, `Rate limit exceeded`, with details and itemId).

500.description: The rate engine failed (v60 106 or a code the mapping does not know, or no response), a rate response carried no SALES_TAX total or an unusable rate (`Unknown API error`), or the API key could not be checked (`Account lookup failed`, with message).

post.description: Calculates sales tax for one or more carts on behalf of a merchant. The request contract is the same for both merchant management modes, so a caller does not have to know which mode a merchant is in. TaxCloud-managed merchant: the request is forwarded to TaxCloud (POST /connections/{connectionId}/carts) using the merchant's stored credentials and TaxCloud's response is returned verbatim; capture the returned cartId with /merchant/order/create-from-cart to record the sale. Self-managed merchant: the cart is calculated in-process by the Ziptax rate engine, US destinations only, and nothing is persisted - the returned cartId correlates the response with the request and cannot be captured as an order, and the other stateful /merchant endpoints return 403. Self-managed calculation rejects (rather than ignores) fields it cannot honour: discounts, exemption, deliveredBySeller, productId, and any currency other than USD. A value that asks for nothing is accepted, so a caller that always emits the TaxCloud shape is not refused: deliveredBySeller false, and an exemption claiming no exemption ({} or {"isExempt": false}). TIC vocabulary also differs: self-managed carts use Ziptax TICs, where 10001 is shipping and 11000 is handling, and TaxCloud's shipping TICs 11010-11015 and the Colorado retail delivery fee TIC 11098 are rejected with 400 because they cannot be mapped onto the in-process shipping and handling treatment. A self-managed cart whose destination address cannot be resolved, for the cart or for a product line's taxability code, returns 422 rather than being quoted at its origin, intrastate as well as interstate: the destination's own sourcing rule decides where a cart is quoted, and an address that did not resolve has none. A self-managed request may contain at most 2500 line items summed across all carts; a larger batch is rejected with 400 before any cart is calculated. Calculation has no lasting side effect in either mode and is safe to retry.

post.description:
Records one or more physical locations for a merchant. A merchant's physical locations are what establish its nexus, and nexus is what decides whether a sale is sourced at its origin or its destination, so this is the data a self-managed cart calculation depends on.

Each address is geocoded as it is written, and the normalized result is what every response returns; expect the address you get back to differ from the one you sent. If any address in the request cannot be resolved to a US state the whole request is rejected with 422 and nothing is stored, so a retry cannot duplicate the locations that would otherwise have succeeded. If the address geocoder is temporarily unavailable the request is rejected with 503 and nothing is stored; it can be retried.

Address resolution for the whole request is budgeted at 10 seconds. A batch that exceeds it returns 504 and stores nothing; send fewer locations per call if you hit this.

Available to self-managed merchants only. A TaxCloud-managed merchant's nexus is held in TaxCloud, so this returns 403 for them.

Removes a recorded location so it no longer contributes to the merchant's nexus. The location stops appearing in /merchant/nexus/list immediately, and is retained internally so past filings keep their basis.

Removing a merchant's last location is allowed: it simply means no physical nexus is tracked for them. Deleting a location that is already gone returns 404.

Available to self-managed merchants only; a TaxCloud-managed merchant returns 403.

Returns a merchant's recorded nexus locations. Deleted locations are not included.

Available to self-managed merchants only; a TaxCloud-managed merchant returns 403, and their nexus is read through the Management API instead.

Replaces a recorded location.

The `location` block is a full replacement, not a patch: every field in it is written, so send the current value for anything you do not want cleared. The address is geocoded again, so an update may change the normalized address even when you send the same string, and a location can be moved to a different state this way. If the address geocoder is temporarily unavailable the update is rejected with 503 and the stored location is unchanged; it can be retried.

post.description:
Updates a merchant's details, its compliance model, or both.

Send `update` to change the merchant's name and contact details, `setMerchantType` to switch the merchant between the `taxcloud` and `self-managed` compliance models, or both together. At least one of the two is required.

Switching the compliance model sets the merchant's `status`: `taxcloud` produces `taxcloud_invited` and emails the merchant a TaxCloud invite, `self-managed` produces `external_compliance`.

**Switching to `self-managed` disconnects the merchant from TaxCloud.** Their stored TaxCloud credentials are removed, so the order, exemption certificate, and refund endpoints return 403 for them and cart calculation switches to Ziptax's own rate engine. Reconnecting later means switching back to `taxcloud` and setting their credentials again via "Set Merchant Credentials".

Sending the compliance model a merchant already has changes nothing and does not re-send the invite, so a request is safe to repeat.

You can only update merchants that belong to your account. Requests for any other merchant, or for one that has been deleted, return 403.

Returns the economic nexus thresholds that decide when a seller has to register in a state: the sales figure, the transaction count where one still applies, how the two combine, which sales count toward them, whether marketplace sales are included, and the period each state measures over.

This is reference data. It is the same for every caller and is not derived from your sales: compare it against your own totals to work out where you are approaching a threshold.

Send no body, or no `stateCodes`, to get every jurisdiction the country publishes. `countryCode` defaults to USA, currently the only country published. States with no general statewide sales tax (Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire, Oregon) are returned with `noSalesTax: true` and null thresholds rather than omitted.

A `stateCodes` list naming a code that is not published is rejected with 400 rather than answered with the states that did match, so a typo cannot read back as 'this state has no threshold'.
